# http1

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/http1"
```

Package http1 is the restricted HTTP/1.1 profile the SDK serves on its loop engine (ADR 0186 §D6): a codec that frames requests out of bytes and appends responses to bytes, and HandleLoop, the adapter that serves a Handler on a loop group of package server.

It is a profile, not an HTTP server, and what it refuses defines it. A request is answered with its status and Connection: close, and its connection closed, before any handler sees it, when it carries any Transfer-Encoding (chunked, and so trailers, included), Expect, a bare CR or LF, a NUL or another control byte in a value, obs-fold, whitespace before a colon, a name outside tchar, a Content-Length that is not one run of at most ten digits or that repeats, a second Authorization or Host, CONNECT, a target two readers could resolve apart — a dot-segment, an empty segment, a backslash, an encoded slash, dot, backslash or NUL, an absolute-form not for its Host — or a head, target or body past its Limits. HTTP/2, Upgrade and TLS are out of the profile: a program that needs them mounts net/http with Group.HandleHTTP. Framing depends on neither the method nor the route: a request takes its head plus its Content-Length.

### Serving

```
type api struct{ lanes []perLane } // one per lane, indexed by Request.Lane

func (a *api) ServeHTTP1(req *http1.Request, res *http1.Response) {
	l := &a.lanes[req.Lane]
	switch req.Route { // set by the router link
	case routeItem:
		res.Defer = true // answered at the end of the batch
		l.pending = append(l.pending, job{res: res, user: req.Auth})
	default:
		res.Status = 404
	}
}

func (a *api) EndBatch(lane int) {
	l := &a.lanes[lane]
	// one transaction for every job of l.pending, then for each:
	// job.res.Status, job.res.Body = ..., ...; job.res.Defer = false
}

routes, _ := http1.Routes(http1.Route{ID: routeItem, Method: "GET", Path: "/items/", Prefix: true},
	http1.Route{ID: routeHealth, Path: "/health"})
bearer, _ := http1.Bearer(verifier, routeHealth) // /health needs no token
srv.Group("api", server.Listen("tcp", ":8080"), server.Loop(server.LoopValue{Loops: 2}), server.Plaintext()).
	HandleLoop(http1.HandleLoop(http1.Chain(a, routes, bearer), http1.Parser{}))
```

A handler runs on its lane's thread and must not block it. Every callback of one lane runs on that thread, one at a time, so state kept per lane needs no lock; Request.Lane and the lane argument of EndBatch name the lane. The answers of a batch leave at its end, in request order on each connection.

### The chain

A link is a Middleware, composed with Chain, the first listed outermost. The codec has already computed the request's canonical Path — no dot-segment, no empty segment, no encoded slash, dot, backslash or NUL, an absolute-form target reduced to its path once its authority matched Host — so every link routes and judges the same bytes. Routes sets Request.Route, Bearer verifies the token for every route its exemptions do not name and copies the subject and the claims into Request.Auth by value, Headers gives every answer its fields, and Log hands an AccessLogger a record of the fields it allows, never a credential. No link writes the bytes a request takes: the adapter frames with what Parse returned.

### The codec alone

Parser.Parse, AppendResponse and AppendRefusal frame and write without the loop, on any \[]byte: nothing allocates once the caller's buffers have room.

<a name="AppendField"></a>
## func [AppendField](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func AppendField(dst []byte, name string, value string) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendField appends "name: value\\r\\n" to dst. A name that is not a token, a control byte in the value, and Content-Length, Connection and Transfer-Encoding, which the codec writes, are refused with ResponseInvalid.

<a name="AppendRefusal"></a>
## func [AppendRefusal](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func AppendRefusal(dst []byte, r Refusal) []byte
```

AppendRefusal appends the whole answer to r — its status, Content-Length: 0 and Connection: close; the caller then closes the connection.

<a name="AppendResponse"></a>
## func [AppendResponse](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func AppendResponse(dst []byte, req *Request, res *Response, closing bool) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendResponse appends the whole answer res gives req: the status line, res.Header, Content-Length from len(res.Body), Connection: close when res, req or closing asks for it, then the body.

<a name="AppendStatusLine"></a>
## func [AppendStatusLine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func AppendStatusLine(dst []byte, status int) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendStatusLine appends the status line of status to dst; below 200 is refused with ResponseInvalid.

<a name="Bearer"></a>
## func [Bearer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Bearer(v BearerVerifier, exempt ...int) (Middleware, error)
```

Bearer returns the authenticating link: a request whose Route is not in exempt is answered 401 unless v verifies its Bearer token; v sets the subject and the claims on the request's Auth, a value.

<a name="CORS"></a>
## func [CORS](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func CORS(cfg CORSValue) (Middleware, error)
```

CORS returns the cross-origin link: a preflight answered 204 by the link, the policy's fields on every other answer, nothing for an origin not listed.

<a name="Canonical"></a>
## func [Canonical](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Canonical(req *Request) Refusal
```

Canonical computes a request's Path and Query from its Target and judges the target, the one reader of a target for a codec that frames some other way: an HTTP/2 request mapped onto a Request, for instance.

<a name="Chain"></a>
## func [Chain](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Chain(h Handler, links ...Middleware) Handler
```

Chain applies links to a handler, outermost first: Chain(h, a, b) yields a(b(h)), the first link listed the first to see a request.

<a name="Continue"></a>
## func [Continue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Continue(buf []byte, req *Request) int
```

Continue returns req.Consumed and sets req.Body once buf holds the whole body of a request whose head Parse framed; until then it returns 0.

<a name="Files"></a>
## func [Files](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Files(route int, fsys fs.FS, cfg static.Config) (Middleware, error)
```

Files returns the link that serves route's file tree on the lane's worker: confined to the tree, a body sent by sendfile or splice, one Range, 304 on the validators. Directories answer their index.html or 404, never a listing.

```go
func HandleLoop(h Handler, p Parser) *LoopHandler
```

HandleLoop adapts h to the loop engine: the handler of server.Group.HandleLoop. p frames every request; the zero Parser is the profile's defaults. A refused request is answered and closed without reaching h; the batch's answers leave at its end, after h's EndBatch when h is a Batcher, in request order on each connection. A Response starts every request with a nil Header and Body, which h points at bytes it owns until the answer is taken. An answer the writer refuses, or one left deferred, is answered 500 and its connection closed; one the connection's output refuses closes the connection.

<a name="Access"></a>
## type [Access](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Access is one request's access-log record, as Log's link hands it to an AccessLogger.

```go
type Access = corenet.HTTP1AccessValue
```

Access is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.HTTP1AccessValue`, declared as:

```go
type Access struct {
	// Lane is the request's lane.
	Lane          int
	// Route is the route a router link matched, zero for none.
	Route         int
	// Method is the request method.
	Method        []byte
	// Path is the request's canonical path, without its query.
	Path          []byte
	// Status is the answer's status code, 200 when the handler left it zero;
	// zero for an answer still deferred.
	Status        int
	// BodyLen is the length of the answer's body.
	BodyLen       int
	// Authenticated reports whether an authenticating link verified the request.
	Authenticated bool
	// TraceID is the trace the request joined, read from its traceparent by a
	// Trace link in the same chain; the zero value without one.
	TraceID       trace.TraceID
	// Stage says what the record is: an answer written, one deferred or pending
	// and so with no status yet, or a deferred answer's completion.
	Stage         HTTP1AccessStage
	// ID is the request's number (HTTP1RequestValue.ID): what a sampling decision
	// or a slow-request record is keyed on, the same on both records of a deferred
	// answer.
	ID            uint64
	// Elapsed is the time from the batch's start to this record, the wait behind
	// the batch's earlier requests included; on a deferred answer's second record
	// the time since it was deferred.
	Elapsed       DurationValue
	// RequestID is the request's correlation identifier, the one its answer
	// carries in X-Request-Id; empty without a RequestID link in the chain.
	RequestID     HTTP1RequestIDValue
	// Proto is the request's HTTP major version, 1 or 2.
	Proto         uint8
	// Stream is the HTTP/2 stream the request arrived on, zero on HTTP/1.1.
	Stream        uint32
	// NFields is how many entries of Fields the record filled.
	NFields       int
	// Fields holds the allowed request fields the request carried, in the order
	// the link was given their names.
	Fields        [8]HTTP1FieldValue
}
```

## type [CORSValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

```go
type CORSValue struct {
	// Origins are the exact origins allowed, as a browser serializes them:
	// scheme://host[:port], in lower case, with no path. "*" allows any origin,
	// alone in the list and without Credentials. "null" is refused: it is what a
	// sandboxed page and a local file both send.
	Origins       []string
	// Methods are the methods a preflight may ask for; empty selects the
	// CORS-safelisted GET, HEAD and POST, never every method.
	Methods       []string
	// Headers are the request fields a preflight may ask for; empty allows only
	// the CORS-safelisted fields.
	Headers       []string
	// ExposeHeaders are the response fields a page may read.
	ExposeHeaders []string
	// Credentials lets a page send cookies and read the answer. It is refused
	// with "*": that combination publishes every user's answers to every site.
	Credentials   bool
	// MaxAge is how long a browser may keep a preflight's answer, clamped to 24
	// hours; zero writes no Access-Control-Max-Age, negative is refused.
	MaxAge        DurationValue
}
```

## type [LoopHandler](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

LoopHandler serves the profile on a loop group: the server.LoopHandler HandleLoop returns.


<a name="LoopHandler.CheckSpill"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [CheckSpill](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop_body.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) CheckSpill(spillCap int) error
```

CheckSpill implements corenet.LoopSpillChecker: Start fails with HTTP1Misconfigured naming body for a Limits.Body the spill cannot hold beside the head, and a default bound is capped at what it can, so a Content-Length past it is refused 413 on the head. A handler that reads bodies as they arrive holds only heads in the spill, and is not bound by it.

<a name="LoopHandler.HTTPCounts"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [HTTPCounts](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) HTTPCounts() corenet.HTTPCountsValue
```

HTTPCounts implements corenet.LoopHTTPCounter: the HTTP/1.1 requests the adapter served, each lane's added at its batch's end; no HTTP/2.

<a name="LoopHandler.MarkServed"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [MarkServed](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) MarkServed(lane int)
```

MarkServed tells the adapter that an adapter embedding it, serving another version on the same lane, served a request of lane's current batch: the next OnBatchEnd then calls the handler's EndBatch even when no HTTP/1.1 request was served, and the embedding adapter does not call it, so a batch that served both versions ends once, as HTTP1Batcher's contract says. It is called on the lane's thread, before OnBatchEnd.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnBatchEnd"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnBatchEnd](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnBatchEnd(io corenet.LoopIO)
```

OnBatchEnd implements corenet.LoopHandler. When the batch served a request — its own, or one MarkServed reported —, it calls the handler's EndBatch if it has one, once, then writes the batch's answers in order and closes the connections whose answer asked to.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnClose"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnClose](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnClose(io corenet.LoopIO, ref corenet.LoopConnRef, err error)
```

OnClose implements corenet.LoopHandler. The connection's held answers are given up — a pending one's job cancelled, its slot freed when it comes back — and its flag stays until the next OnOpen of its slot replaces it; an answer of the batch still queued for it is dropped when its Write is refused as stale.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnData"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnData](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnData(io corenet.LoopIO, ref corenet.LoopConnRef, buf []byte) int
```

OnData implements corenet.LoopHandler. It frames every whole request at the start of buf, serves each in turn, and returns the bytes they took: a request still incomplete waits in the loop's spill for its next bytes. A refused request, or one whose answer closes the connection, takes the rest of buf, which is never read.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnDone"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnDone](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop_pending.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnDone(io corenet.LoopIO, job corenet.LoopJobValue)
```

OnDone implements corenet.LoopOffloader, on the lane's thread: the job's answer is ready, and its connection is flushed at the batch's end, in request order. A connection that closed meanwhile has its slot freed and nothing written.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnDrain"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnDrain](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/stream.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnDrain(io corenet.LoopIO, ref corenet.LoopConnRef)
```

OnDrain implements corenet.LoopDrainer: a connection streaming a response is told through its HTTP1Streamer; any other is left to the drain.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnOpen"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnOpen](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnOpen(io corenet.LoopIO, ref corenet.LoopConnRef)
```

OnOpen implements corenet.LoopHandler. It marks the connection open on its lane.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnOutbound"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnOutbound](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop_pending.go>)

```go

```

OnOutbound implements corenet.LoopOffloader: each lane keeps its outbound, and every connection's holdback is bounded by the output ceiling.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnStart"></a>
### func \(LoopHandler\) [OnStart](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/loop.go>)

```go
func (*LoopHandler) OnStart(lanes int)
```

OnStart implements corenet.LoopStarter: it builds every lane's state before the first callback, so no lane builds its own under a lock.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnTimeout"></a>

```go

```

OnTimeout implements corenet.LoopHandler. The adapter arms no deadline, so a timeout it did not ask for closes the connection.

<a name="LoopHandler.OnWritable"></a>


OnWritable implements corenet.LoopHandler. Nothing waits on it: an answer the output refuses closes its connection.

<a name="LoopHandler.Pending"></a>

<a name="LoopHandler.Unwrap"></a>

Unwrap returns the HTTP1Handler the adapter serves: what tells a loop group that its handler speaks the codec, so it may take TLS on the portable backend (ADR 0187 §D5).

<a name="Parser"></a>
## type [Parser](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Parser frames requests under its Limits. The zero Parser uses the profile's defaults; NewParser validates others.

```go
type Parser = svchttp1.Parser
```

Parser is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/net/http1.Parser`, declared as:

```go
type Parser struct{}
```

<a name="Parser.Limits"></a>
### func \(Parser\) [Limits](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/parse.go>)

```go
func (Parser) Limits() corenet.HTTP1LimitsValue
```

Limits returns the bounds the Parser applies, defaults resolved.

<a name="Parser.Parse"></a>
### func \(Parser\) [Parse](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/http1/parse.go>)

```go
func (Parser) Parse(buf []byte, req *corenet.HTTP1RequestValue) (int, Refusal)
```

Parse frames the request at the start of buf into req and returns the bytes it takes and RefusalNone, once the whole request is there.

It returns 0 and RefusalNone while more bytes are needed. When the head is complete and only the body is missing, req.HeadLen and req.Consumed are already set: Continue then waits for the body without reading the head again, and an early answer knows how much the request still has to send.

It returns 0 and the refusal when the bytes break the profile. A refusal never depends on bytes past the one that broke a rule, so more bytes never turn it into an acceptance; and an accepted request takes the same bytes whatever follows it, the next pipelined request included.

Framing depends on neither the method nor the target: a request takes its head plus its Content-Length, a GET's included. Every slice in req aliases buf. Parse allocates nothing.

<a name="Request"></a>
## type [Request](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Request is one request, framed by the codec. Every slice aliases the bytes Request is one request, framed by the codec. Every slice aliases the bytes it was framed from; Lane names the lane that framed it, Path is its canonical path, Route and Auth what the chain's links set.

```go
type Request = corenet.HTTP1RequestValue
```

Request is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.HTTP1RequestValue`, declared as:

```go
type Request struct {
	// Method is the request method, a token.
	Method           []byte
	// Target is the request-target exactly as sent, still percent-encoded.
	Target           []byte
	// Host is the Host field's value; HasHost says whether it was present.
	Host             []byte
	// Authorization is the Authorization field's value; HasAuthorization says
	// whether it was present.
	Authorization    []byte
	// Body is the request content, Content-Length bytes after the head. It is
	// empty until the whole body has arrived.
	Body             []byte
	// ContentLength is the declared body length, zero when the field is absent.
	ContentLength    int64
	// HeadLen is the length of the head: the request line, the field lines and
	// the blank line. It is zero until the head is complete.
	HeadLen          int
	// Consumed is HeadLen plus ContentLength: the bytes this request takes from
	// the stream, whatever its method or route. The next pipelined request
	// starts there. It is set as soon as the head is complete, before the body
	// arrives, so an early answer knows how much it has to drain.
	Consumed         int
	// NFields is how many entries of Fields the request filled.
	NFields          int
	// Fields holds the request's field lines in the order they arrived,
	// Host, Authorization and Content-Length included.
	Fields           [64]HTTP1FieldValue
	// HasHost reports whether the request carried a Host field.
	HasHost          bool
	// HasAuthorization reports whether the request carried an Authorization
	// field.
	HasAuthorization bool
	// Close reports whether the client asked to close the connection after
	// this request: a Connection field holding the close token.
	Close            bool
	// Lane is the index of the lane that framed the request, from 0 to the
	// group's lane count less one — its LoopIO.Loop — set by the loop adapter
	// before the handler runs. One lane is one thread or one goroutine, so a
	// handler finds its per-lane state in a slice sized at LoopStarter.OnStart,
	// with no lock. Parse leaves it as it is; outside the loop adapter it is
	// what the caller set.
	Lane             int
	// Path is the request's canonical path, the one target every link of a
	// chain routes and judges on, computed once by the codec: the target's
	// path up to its query, an absolute-form target reduced to its path once
	// its authority matched Host. It is still percent-encoded, and holds no
	// dot-segment, no empty segment, no backslash and no encoded slash, dot,
	// backslash or NUL: the codec refuses a target that would (400). An
	// asterisk-form target, OPTIONS only, is "*".
	Path             []byte
	// Query is the target's query, after its "?" and without it; empty when
	// the target has none.
	Query            []byte
	// Route is the identifier of the route a router link matched, zero for
	// none. Parse resets it to zero; only a link sets it.
	Route            int
	// Auth is what an authenticating link established: the subject and the
	// claims, copied by value into the request, so nothing of them aliases
	// bytes the connection reuses. Parse resets it; Authenticated says
	// whether a link set it.
	Auth             HTTP1AuthValue
	// Authenticated reports whether an authenticating link verified the
	// request's credentials and filled Auth. Parse resets it to false.
	Authenticated    bool
	// Trace is the request's W3C trace context, as the http1 chain's Trace link
	// read it from the traceparent field: invalid (IsValid false) when no such
	// link ran, when the field is absent, or when it is malformed, a request
	// being served either way (§4.3). tracestate is not read: a request carries
	// the 25 bytes of the context and no list. Parse resets it.
	Trace            trace.SpanContextValue
	// Scheme is the :scheme pseudo-field of an HTTP/2 request, empty on HTTP/1.1.
	// An HTTP/2 codec maps a request before Canonical (ADR 0220): Method from
	// :method; Target from :path, origin-form or "*" (an absolute-form :path is
	// RefusalTargetForm); Host from :authority, else the Host field, both present
	// and different RefusalTargetHost, HasHost set; Fields the regular fields in
	// arrival order with HPACK's lowercase names; Authorization, ContentLength and
	// Body as on HTTP/1.1; Close, HeadLen and Consumed zero.
	Scheme           []byte
	// Proto is the request's HTTP major version, 1 or 2.
	Proto            uint8
	// Stream is the HTTP/2 stream the request arrived on, zero on HTTP/1.1.
	Stream           uint32
	// ID identifies the request on its lane — the lane in the top 16 bits, a
	// counter from 1 in the rest — set by the loop adapter before the handler
	// runs, so two lanes never hold the same one. It is a number the client
	// never sees, what a sampling decision or a slow-request record is keyed on.
	// Parse leaves it as it is; outside the loop adapter it is what the caller
	// set.
	ID               uint64
	// Conn names the connection the request arrived on, set by the loop adapter
	// before the handler runs: what a handler keeps to find, at
	// HTTP1Streamer.OnStreamOpen, the stream this request opened. Parse leaves it
	// as it is.
	Conn             LoopConnRef
	// RoutePrefix is how many leading bytes of Path the Prefix route a router link
	// matched covers, zero for an exact route or none: what a file tree strips to
	// find the name under its route. Parse resets it; only a link sets it.
	RoutePrefix      int
	// RequestID is the request's correlation identifier, as the http1 chain's
	// RequestID link accepted it from X-Request-Id or minted it: copied by
	// value, so a handler that needs it past the batch copies this value into
	// its own job table. Parse resets it; it is empty when no such link ran.
	RequestID        HTTP1RequestIDValue
}
```

<a name="Request.Field"></a>
### func \(Request\) [Field](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/http1.go>)


### func \(RequestIDValue\) [Set](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/http1_auth.go>)

```go
func (*RequestIDValue) Set(b []byte) bool
```

Set copies b into the value and reports true, or leaves the value as it is and reports false when b is empty, longer than HTTP1MaxRequestID or holds a byte outside 0x21 to 0x7E: the codec writes the value into a response head, so what the wire cannot carry never enters it.

<a name="Response"></a>
## type [Response](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Response is the answer a Handler gives: a status, extra field lines written by AppendField, a body, Close, and Defer to answer at the batch's end.

```go
type Response = corenet.HTTP1ResponseValue
```

Response is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.HTTP1ResponseValue`, declared as:

```go
type Response struct {
	// Status is the status code, 200 to 999; zero means 200. The profile
	// sends no interim response.
	Status     int
	// Header holds the response's extra field lines, each written as
	// "Name: value\r\n" by the codec's writer. It never holds Content-Length or
	// Connection, which the codec writes.
	Header     []byte
	// Body is the response content.
	Body       []byte
	// Close asks the codec to close the connection after this response.
	Close      bool
	// Defer, set by the handler, holds the answer back until the end of the
	// loop's batch, for work it batches — one database transaction for every
	// request of the batch, say. The response value then stays valid, at the
	// same address, until HTTP1Batcher.EndBatch returns, and the handler
	// completes it there: it fills it and clears Defer. An answer still
	// deferred when EndBatch returns is answered 500 and its connection
	// closed. Only the loop adapter reads it; AppendResponse does not.
	Defer      bool
	// Pending, set by the handler, hands the answer to the lane's worker
	// (HTTP1Worker, R3): the loop adapter sends Job to it and writes the
	// answer the worker fills, from the loop's thread, once it comes back.
	// Answers after it on the same connection wait for it, in order. A queue
	// to the worker that is full answers 503 with Retry-After at once, the
	// connection kept; a connection that closes first drops the answer. Pending
	// with Defer, or with no worker, is answered 500 and the connection closed.
	// Only the loop adapter reads it.
	Pending    bool
	// Job is the integer a pending answer's worker is given: the handler's own
	// index of what the work needs, which it copied out of the request, since
	// the request's bytes do not outlive the batch.
	Job        uint64
	// TraceLine holds the traceparent field line the http1 chain's Trace link
	// writes on this answer, Header pointing at it; a value, so a deferred
	// answer keeps it past the request. Only the link sets it.
	TraceLine  [70]byte
	// RequestID is the identifier the codec writes as an X-Request-Id field after
	// Header, when set: a value, so a deferred or a pending answer keeps it past
	// the request, and a field written per request needs no slice to outlive the
	// batch. The chain's RequestID link sets it.
	RequestID  HTTP1RequestIDValue
	// Stream answers with a response delimited by the connection's close (RFC 9112
	// §6.3 item 8): the codec writes the status line and the fields with
	// Connection: close and no Content-Length, refusing HEAD, 204 and 304 with
	// HTTP1ResponseInvalid, and the handler keeps writing the body through
	// HTTP1Streamer. Requests pipelined behind it are dropped with the connection.
	// A Stream with Defer or Pending, behind a held answer, or with no
	// HTTP1Streamer in the handler is answered 500 and the connection closed. It
	// does not make a chunked answer: ADR 0186 §D6 still refuses every coding.
	Stream     bool
	// Upgrade answers 101 Switching Protocols: the codec writes the status line,
	// Connection: Upgrade and Header — which holds the protocol's own fields —
	// and no length, then every later byte of the connection goes to
	// HTTP1Upgrader. It carries no body; with one, or with no HTTP1Upgrader in the
	// handler, the answer is 500 and the connection closed.
	Upgrade    bool
	// RetryAfter, when above zero, is written by the codec as a Retry-After field
	// in seconds after Header: a value, so a refusal needs no slice of its own.
	// The chain's RateLimit link sets it.
	RetryAfter int
	// CORS holds the field lines the chain's CORS link gives this answer, written
	// by the codec after Header: its own slot, so the link costs nothing beside a
	// Headers link, and its bytes are the policy's, shared and read only.
	CORS       []byte
	// File, set by a pending answer's worker, makes the answer's body a file: the
	// codec writes the head with Content-Length File.Len and no body bytes, and
	// sends the file behind it. A HEAD answer closes File.R unsent. With Body, on a
	// 204 or a 304, or outside a worker's answer it is answered 500 and the
	// connection closed.
	File       HTTP1FileValue
}
```

## type [Route](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Route is one route of Routes' link: an identifier, a method, a canonical path and whether it is a prefix.

```go
type Route = svchttp1.RouteValue
```

Route is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/net/http1.RouteValue`, declared as:

```go
type Route struct {
	// ID identifies the route, from 1; zero is "no route".
	ID     int
	// Method is the method the route takes, empty for any.
	Method string
	// Path is the canonical path the route matches, from "/": the whole of
	// it, or its start when Prefix is set.
	Path   string
	// Prefix makes Path match the start of a request's path, on a segment
	// boundary: "/health" matches "/health" and "/health/live", never
	// "/healthz"; a Path ending in "/" matches whatever follows it.
	Prefix bool
}
```

<a name="Worker"></a>
## type [Worker](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/http1/gen_facade.go>)

Worker is the optional capability of a Handler served on a loop group that answers off the loop's thread: a Response marked Pending is filled by WorkHTTP1 on the lane's worker goroutine, which may block, and written once it returns.

```go
}
```
